today.name: Ayven
today.tagline: Carries and drives your team's agenda
today.description: Ayven drives your agenda. It means observing, cutting the work into pieces your team can take one at a time, putting an owner and a date on each, and filing them in Jira or YouTrack. Then it runs, tracks and talks about the work for weeks: asking whoever knows, waiting, chasing silence, moving work when someone is away. Your team answers in Slack and the board moves. Planning stops being the barrier and you ship your agenda like crazy.

comments.text: Howard here, founder of Alknoma.We didn't start with a product. We started with an ANNOYANCE. Agents were impressive while you were talking to them, and then, as soon as you stopped typing, they effectively disappeared.You'd put one in Slack and end up with another bot sitting in a channel waiting for someone to tell it what to do.You don't prompt your teammates.So the real problem was never, "How do we make the model smarter?" It was: how do you give a language model a spine? Something that lets it chain call after call, across days and months, reaching out to different people, all without a human babysitting it.Sounds impossible if you know from experience just how complex chaining LLM calls can be. Three things turned out to matter, and we learned each one the painful way.1. What a piece of work actually is.Small enough that it can be validated, iterated, executed and closed 99.9% of the time.Too big and the agent starts hallucinating. Too small and it loses all semantic meaning.2. Resolving time should be first-class.A lot of work in a team is essentially waiting.Waiting isn't failure. It's the norm. And that happens to be one of the things LLM agents are worst at. Ayven reasons about when it should wake up next, EVERY SINGLE TIME, across thousands of runs a week.It is about recognising a deadline, annual leave, or when a teammate has gone quiet. The async gap is hard to nail down. Ayven does that.3. What is the base unit of a fact.In a team, things change constantly. Someone changes their mind, a deadline moves, a customer replies, a meeting gets cancelled. An agent would treat information that was true two days ago as gospel. Change is the critical signal, and that was difficult to implement when teamwork is so unpredictable. Ayven makes sure the right things change with it.The magic moment that wowed us, and made us decide to launch Ayven: we gave Ayven the agenda for September. Nothing else. The next thing we knew, the board was full, and accurate to our plans. It put together the pieces of what execution would look like.Later, I asked: "What's stopping us from launching on Product Hunt?" Ayven then told me about every dependencies that I did not previously know. Nobody wrote that answer. It was just the work being captured in its truest, current state.There is a lot more to Ayven that we haven't covered here.Talk to us if you want this deployed in your own environment. Tell us what you want it connected to.Ask me anything :)

comments.text: Hi everyone!Google Japan's Gboard team keeps coming up with wonderfully odd keyboard ideas, and it has become a yearly tradition. week.name: ReSO AI
week.tagline: Get discovered & recommended when customers ask AI
week.description: ReSO is a generative engine optimization platform that helps brands show up in AI search results. It’s built for founders, CMOs, and growth teams who want to turn buyer intent in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AIO into visibility, citations, and traffic. comments.text: 👋 Hey Product Hunt!I'm Swati, Co-founder of ReSO!Having led marketing across B2B, B2C for 2 decades, organic has been my favorite revenue growth channel. In that moment every brand which is not in the answer loses a potential customer.The problem: When we started auditing brands, we kept finding the same thing; companies ranking on page 1 of Google that were near-invisible in AI answers, losing recommendations to smaller competitors. We treat measurement as step one, not the product. The product is the movement from unmentioned, to cited, to recommended. ReSO is your company’s employee who takes ownership of results.Who its for: Founders, SEO & content teams, and agencies who can see search shifting and want a system & not another report to win it.🎁 For the PH community: Free AI visibility audit of your brand & 100% off one month access for launch-week signups worth USD 599🙏 Our ask: Honest feedback over upvotes. Tell me when your buyers ask AI about your category, do you know if you show up? Drop your site in the comments and I'll share what we find. I'll be here all day.Big shout-out to my small but relentless team who turned this from a spreadsheet obsession into a product and thank you @jonnotie, the PH team, and this community for the platform to share it.@shubhangi_goyal @aanchal_dahiya @dayal_punjabi

week.name: Onepin
week.tagline: AI voiceover with every name, price and date said right
week.description: AI voices sound human now. But they still guess names from the spelling, and nobody has time to listen to every line. Onepin runs on the voices you already use (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, 30+ more), spells out prices and dates, checks names against a 4M-word pronunciation dictionary, scores every line, and fixes the wrong word without re-rendering the take. Built for teams shipping AI voiceover in several languages: product videos, dubbing, courses. Free to start, no credit card required.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 SB here, founder of Onepin. Thanks @rohanrecommends for hunting us.A great AI voice reads "Porsche Taycan" as TAY-can. Porsche says TIE-kahn. It guessed from the spelling, and nobody caught it, because nobody listens to line 1,200.We spent two years at Podonos measuring how AI voices sound, with 150,000 human listeners doing the rating. The models solved delivery. What kept failing was names, prices and dates, and the only check most teams run is a person with headphones.Today we're launching Onepin, the production step after text-to-speech. It runs on the voices you already use, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google and 30+ more, and checks every line before it ships.Here is what it does to every script:🔢 Spells out prices, dates and abbreviations before the voice reads them.📖 Checks names, brands and drug terms against a 4-million-word pronunciation dictionary.📊 Scores every line for naturalness, clarity, word accuracy and pronunciation, against a bar you set.🔧 Fixes the one wrong word in the same voice, without re-rendering the take.Two decisions we made on purpose. Onepin checks how a name was said, not just what the transcript spells. And there is no box where you type phonetic spellings: the dictionary and the fix do that work, so your script stays as written.Built for anyone shipping AI voiceover at volume: product videos, ads, explainers, dubbing, audiobooks, courses, and platforms that put a voice in front of millions of users. API, SDK and MCP from day one. SOC 2 Type II.You keep your voice. Onepin makes sure it says the right words.Free to start, no card: onepin.ai. You can run one line on the homepage without an account.Try it and tell me what's missing, here or at sb@onepin.ai. We'll be in the comments all day, answering questions and running your lines. 🚀🎁 LAUNCH SPECIAL: 20% off for Product Hunt users through October 31. The code is under the 20% off badge above.One question for you: what's the word your AI voice keeps getting wrong? Run it on onepin.ai (free, no card), switch the run to shareable, and paste the link below so everyone can hear the before and after. I'll reply to every one. No time to sign up? week.aiReview: مسئله اصلی این است که کاربران فعلی مجبورند هوش مصنوعی را به‌عنوان یک ابزار جانبی استفاده کنند که باعث ایجاد اصطکاک در جریان کار می‌شود. راه‌حل OpenSwarm، یکپارچه‌سازی عمیق عامل‌های هوشمند در لایه سیستم عامل است تا اپلیکیشن‌ها و مرورگرها به‌صورت خودکار عمل کنند. از نظر معماری، این محصول بر روی هماهنگی چندعاملی (Multi-agent Orchestration) و مدیریت وضعیت (State Management) برای جلوگیری از تداخل عملیات تمرکز دارد. مدل درآمدی احتمالی شامل اشتراک‌های B۲C برای توسعه‌دهندگان و لایسنس‌های سازمانی B۲B است. نقاط قوت شامل تغییر پارادایم از «اجرا» به «هماهنگی» و افزایش چشمگیر بهره‌وری است. نقاط ضعف اصلی شامل پیچیدگی بالای مدیریت تداخل عملیات‌های غیرایده‌مپوتانت (مانند ارسال پیام یا فرم) و نگرانی‌های امنیتی در مورد دسترسی کامل عامل‌ها به دستگاه است. نکته طلایی برای ایران: با توجه به محدودیت‌های دسترسی به مدل‌های خارجی، توسعه نسخه‌ای که از مدل‌های زبانی محلی یا خود میزبان (Self-hosted) استفاده کند و روی امنیت داده‌های محلی (Local-first) تأکید ویژه‌ای داشته باشد، می‌تواند مزیت رقابتی قوی در بازار داخلی ایجاد کند.

Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
